messages.content:
The Lore™

PART 1
THE WORLD’S CONFLICT

The Mythos
Two twin sisters: Alysane and Aila
Aila- relies on strength, raw power, resilience, and emotion
Alysane - relies on knowledge, numbers, and strategy
They HATE each other
Thought they would be allowed to rule one world alone, but have to rule together
They hate each other for it and want the other to die


Fight club: god edition
First, they tried to fight each other
Here’s what some of their scuffles caused in the world:
Their first physical altercation - the continent split in two.
Their second - had the waters rise to flood the continents. 
Another fight - flattened the majority of the southernmost tip of another continent
No real life, just desert.
Clearly, it wasn’t working
They can’t die with their magic, and they’re gods. It’s gonna take more effort to kill each other.


The Bet
They were going to destroy their world if they didn’t stop, so they came up with a plan
Each sister would allow some of their magic into the world (AKA into the inhabitants).
The sister that “won” would be the one with surviving spawn.
If they lost they would abandon their control on the world (aka die willingly).
They agreed, and began crafting their “perfect” spawn…

The Magic
Four central tenets of magic
Elemental Manipulation - think Avatar but expanded
Mind Mastery - telepathy, teleportation, telekinesis, etc.
Body Mastery - shapeshifting, immortality/expanded lifespans, supernatural physical abilities
Life/Death - control over creating new life or being a harbinger of death (or bringing people back by walking the balance)
Emotionally connected
It draws on the power of emotions
The angrier, happier, and the sadder they are, the more powerful they are. 
Use too much? You’ll feel numb for a long, long time.



Aila’s Plan
Aila knew power wasn’t unlimited
She decided to give her magic to a select few so they could remain powerful.
*It would also keep her powerful.
Each spawn would only get access to one tenet of magic
They could not access magic outside of that tenet (a person with mastery over the body couldn’t obtain mastery of the mind, etc.)
Each tenet got a range of spawn, some having more than others.
Life/Death only had one to two spawn, while there were hundreds with power over the mind.
Insanely powerful and able to specialize in one aspect of magic, making them lethal.

 

Ailaspawn
Aila chose her spawn carefully, and they had to meet her standards. 
Most were strong in their mind before they were gifted powers
They tended to have:
Rough childhoods they overcame
Difficult circumstances magic could solve (like major physical disabilities)
Very emotional/have access to their emotions (for more power)
Most were battle-tested and vetted through trauma. 
If angry, these spawn can cause geographical/weather-based catastrophes.
Many were overemotional, and too many emotions can lead to a massive wave of magic followed by prolonged numbness.
Their magic is a feature inside of them that intertwines with emotions, so if one isn’t used it can influence/bleed into another.

Alysane’s plan
Alysane knew that numbers mattered more than specialized warriors.
She also wanted her magic to be accessible to anyone willing to join the fight. 
Her thoughts: “once they win the war I can just steal Aila’s magic.”
The trials for Alysane:
If anyone wanted access to magic, they could complete these trials to obtain power.
They were very difficult in the beginning, but there was a higher reward (stronger power).
You also had to agree to her rules:
You must never KILL another being. 
You must fight for Alysane and her causes.
Many people decided to try her trials, and tens of thousands succeeded.

Alysane-spawn
These folks are from any walks of life
Academics, war heroes, peasants, etc. 
The general traits of the people who passed the trials were:
Intelligent/Perceptive
Charismatic
Loyal
The pull the magic from other people and the earth, NOT from themselves
Can rely on: other people’s emotions, magical items/hotspots (where Alysane appeared in the world), etc.
The trials (at the beginning of the war) were a strong vetting process
As history progressed, the trials moved from multiple stages to a promise.
You must swear to never kill another soul.
You must fight for Alysane’s cause.
These promises, people found, were easy to bend/work around…

The Loophole
Many Alysane-spawn didn’t care about following the first rule.
To fight for Alysane’s cause, they would have to kill Ailaspawn. 
It was hard to fight against specialized and rageful soldiers WITHOUT aiming to kill.
So, they did their best to circumvent the rules.
AKA, Monster Creation 

Magical Byproducts
Made from revenge, desperation, or envy
Alysane spawns created the first monsters, or magical byproducts: the serpents.
Alysane spawn created more and more species from the bodies of Ailaspawn to bypass the killing rule
These monsters had low cognition and had only two purposes (eat and reproduce)
The Ailaspawn with the ability to tap into life/death weren’t interested in making new species
However, after too many deaths/creations, they made high cognition byproducts.
Examples: werewolves and vampires. 
Still caveats, and still unable to tap into the power of Aila, but these byproducts had more control and were able to establish communities. 
Wolves ran into the Northern Mountains
Vampires assimilated throughout the Western country. 

The Magical Hierarchy
Ailaspawn is over Alysane-spawn
Aila’s creations are over Alysane’s creations
Gods
Magic
Wielders
Magical 
Byproducts
Humans

Magical Genetics 101
Obviously people have survived for a while, like centuries upon centuries. 
So, here’s how magic passes down:
Ailaspawn:
Ailaspawn can only obtain their magic through genetics, and it’s not as potent as it was for their parent. 
However, Aila will occasionally choose someone new to give magic (based on her discretion).
Still way more powerful than Alysane-spawn.
Alysane-spawn:
They can pass their magic down (which is still not as potent as it was for their parent) or obtain it through a trial. 
Alysane’s magic is extremely drained after centuries of this, which means the less magic there is to pool from. 
Most spawn have very little access to pull from.

Main Overview of Part 1
Two goddesses, Aila and Alysane
Hate each other and want the other dead, so they made a bet with each other.
Ailaspawn - super powerful, specialized, and overly emotional
Alysane-spawn - abundant, able to access all tenets of magic, have to draw on other things for magic. 
Both have versions of byproducts: Alysane’s (low cognition) and Aila’s (high cognition)
Magic has faded through the centuries, but still present
More so with Aila than with Alysane

Part 2
THE WORLD’S GEOGRAPHY 

The Results of the War
Continent 1 (where the story takes place)
The war has been almost completed, with only two known Ailaspawn on the continent (the two main characters)
In actuality, these are not the only Ailaspawn, as there are:
Shapeshifters who assimilated in the wolf tribes (the Northernmost country)
Elves (other shapeshifters and mind magic folks) hidden in the East
Most people don’t care about the Ailaspawn that survive, as they help with another major issue on the continent (will be addressed later)
Continent 2 (later on in the story)
This continent is fucking INSANE. 
Constant war and no one is ever really winning. 
A lot of fucked up shit still happens (as this is where Aila and Alysane focus their attention on). 
This one isn’t planned out as much but know its a massive war and isn’t addressed until way later.

Continent 1: FAFO
Funnily enough, turning all of your enemies into literal monsters is not a good idea!
The monsters consistently aim to kill literally anything breathing, as that is their purpose. 
Many humans and Alysane spawn are not equipped to handle killing these beasts. 
Alysane spawn can lose their magic, and even if they don’t care about that, they don’t have enough magic to kill them
Many of the low cognition monsters are easy to kill with swords and enhanced/supernatural abilities, but there’s so many that people get overwhelmed. 
Continent 1 has a couple of things to try and get rid of the ever-growing population

Who You Gonna Call?
There are a couple of private mercenaries that target specific monsters
Decades of training and hunting allow them to make money, but many don’t live long.
They also almost never get to retire (they end up dying eventually)
Not nearly enough private people to kill this many beasts. 
Second plan: the counties have a group huddle
They need to find a way to deal with the monsters without killing important people. 
So, an idea is formed: The Sisterhood.


The Sisterhood
There are many Alysane-spawn that come into their power when they’re young.
The Sisterhood seeks to prey on this: they take the women into their keeps, train them to hunt down these byproducts, and then send them out with an indenture.
How do they indenture them?
Easy! The Sisterhood charges for each year in the keep. For however long you’re there, that’s how long you have to fight these monsters. 
Five years in the keep is about the average. 
There’s a monetary value that’s almost impossible for an average spawn to pay. 
This allows rich folks to send their kids to learn how to harness magic WITHOUT having their children die (fucked up, right?)

Okay, but…
Now, why would the Sisterhood train Alysane-spawn to kill if they could lose their magic because of it?
Answer: a loophole! (Alysane spawn are great at figuring these out)
Technically, they can’t kill anything with their magic. Without is fine.
This was found out by one of the original Sisters of the Sisterhood, who successfully stabbed and killed a serpent without losing their magic. 
Completely changed the game for Alysane spawn. 

Teachings of the Sisterhood
They teach about four main classes:
Swordsmanship/Weaponry
Basically just how to hold your own in battle without magic.
Magical Healing/Support Magic
How to use your magic to heal, or create items (such as poisons) that can kill these beasts.
History/Mythical Zoology
What monsters exist and their weak points. Also which ones to approach and which ones not to approach. 
Basic Reading/Writing/Arithmetic
Just so they can function in society, not so they can think enough to fight back. 

Hierarchy/Geography of the Sisterhood
Hierarchy
Praeta- leader of the keep
One for each keep, and there is one major leader per country. 
There are three that form a council, where big decisions are made. 
Sisters who complete their training can become trainers, helping the next generation survive.
Geography
Scattered all throughout the continent, especially in countries that encourage magic usage. 
Most prominent in the West, but there are many scattered in the East. 
The south has a few but the majority of the land can be uninhabitable for byproducts. 
The North has a strong anti-magic stance, so there are none in the North. 
The monsters either live long enough to attack a village, or they die in the extreme cold.

Country/Geography Overview
There are four countries in the Continent:
Laskavo- the northernmost country
Capital - Zhertva (sacrifice for your country)
Leader- King
Kalosori - the westward country
Capital - Nike (victory)
Leader - elected leader from noble council
Huanying - the eastward country
Capital - Pingheng (balance)
Leader- King/Emperor but council that is democratically elected.
Svaagat Karana- the southernmost country 
Capital - Chamatkaar (marvel)
Leader- just a council (elected from nobles)

Country Deep Dive: Svaagat Karana
Based on Indian (South Asian) culture.
There is a lot of uninhabitable land (as this is where that fight between the gods took place)
The desert is known as the Maut
How do they get around this? Easy! Canals
Built by one of its founders, the desert is littered with canals that help water traverse through every part of the country
The canals are called Zindagee
They are everywhere in their cities and their lands, and allow for booming trade.
Notable cities: 
Chamatkaar (marvel), Gyaan (knowledge, in honor of Alysane), and Aasha (hope).

Country Deep Dive: Huanying
Based heavily on Chinese culture.
Most advanced of the four countries in terms of tech, and the balance between science and magic. 
They also aim to find peace between the two goddesses and their spawn (all spawn are welcome regardless of their origins). 
The Mountains of Luan
Where some Ailaspawn live, specifically powerful elven creatures who never emerge in the cities (at least that people are aware)
Very populated, not leaving a lot of space for new people
Noteable cities: Heping (peace), Pingheng (balance), and Jinbu (the promise of progress).

Country Deep Dive: Kalosori
Based on Greco-Roman culture (also where the story starts out)
Knowledge is the most important thing, above all 
So, there also MAJOR alysane defenders, but all are pretty neutral
This is where the majority of wielders come from (who are specifically descended from Alysane)
This is also where there are the most monsters
Notable cities: Malthisi (learning, in honor of Alysane), Synesse (in honor of Alysane’s wisdom), and Nike (in honor of Alysane’s victory for the continent)

Country Deep Dive: Laskavo
Based heavily on Russian culture. 
Like Svaagat Karana, the land is mostly uninhabitable (cold wastelands instead of desert)
However, they don’t care about innovation, rather suffering through things. 
There’s sitll only about ten cities that the leader overlooks
The only other inhabitants are the wolves in the North East Mountain Range (Voyk Range)
These wolves are in deep civil war with the leader.
They also can withstand the cold (due to their creation and evolution)
Notable cities: Vidprava (duty to your country comes first), Virnist (loyalty to your country), and Zhertva (sacrifice for your country).

Diplomatic Interactions
All keep away from the North, but trade with each others. 
Each country has specific exports and imports that they trade within each other
The south trades magically modified crops and livestock grown next to/because of the canals.
Tourism is also booming for SK, as the canals are a marvel of that continent.
The east trades a lot of luxury goods, as well as technology.
Immigration is a very big business for the East.
The west’s primary trade is knowledge and Sisters (from the Sisterhood)
The Sisterhood is in fact their biggest money maker.
The North takes none of the trades, only keeping within itself. It doesn’t allow people to leave the North. 
It’s a really shitty place. People can flee and seek asylum in the East/South and be accepted, if they can make it that far. 

Main Overview of Part 2
Continent 1 got FUCKED over by the war and Alysane-spawn
They corrected with the Sisterhood, a basic human trafficking ring.
It became it’s own cult-like society with a hierarchy, and ultimately became a commodity.
Four countries: Laskavo, Kalosori, Huanying, and Svaagat Karana
The west, east, and south have their problems but benefit its civilians
The same cannot be said about the North

Part 3
THE PROTAGONISTS

Aequia - Broad Overview 
The main protagonist of the story
Ailaspawn (elemental manipulation)
When the story begins:
25-26 years old
Has completed her indenture and is actively training new recruits in swordsmanship
Hates the Sisterhood but when she planned on leaving, another Ailaspawn appeared.
Desperately wants a family, as she has none. 
Currently in a Western country Keep. 

Aequia - Background
Grew up in the Western kingdom
In a village until she was 6, then the Sisterhood
Almost got burned alive in her village bc they hated her and she might’ve flooded their town. 
Her parents? Dead. Anyone who loves her? Dead. RIP
She has no idea where she’s truly from
Everyone around her wasn’t indigenous/looked like her, and she is originally not from Continent 1. 
She finds out she’s from Continent 2 and was shipped over to save her from the war.
Had a ten year indenture to the Sisterhood, completed it in six
She made so much money doing it that she paid it off, which is almost unheard of in the Sisterhood. 

Aequia - Physical Characteristics 
Modern indigenous woman
Dark long hair, usually up in some manner
Beginning of the story - up in a ponytail and/or bun
End of the story - a braid or two, as to denote her culture (which is not known to her until near the end of the series)
Tall, like over six foot tall, and very muscular 
Usually wears training clothes that consistently get dirty
Twin swords strapped to her hips
Armor reveals her arms, which allows better use of her magic. 

Aequia- Emotional and Behavioral Characteristics 
She is very emotional (and therefore very powerful)
Consistently knows how to weave through her emotions to make a point, though sometimes she has moments where they take over
This is normal for Ailaspawn
She is very outspoken about what’s wrong
This goes for both the Sisterhood and anything else she deems immoral
This gets her into a LOT of shit, because she doesn’t know when to shut up with it LMFAO
She is very prone to violence when protecting someone
Goes for anyone she deems as a threat
However, her protectiveness can blind her from seeing someone’s potential. 

Aequia - Plot Relevance
She’s the main character so she’s got a LOT of relevance
She goes on the main mission to protect someone she sees as weak (Gaia). 
She learns about some really dangerous monsters, and is one of the only people competent enough to kill them. 
She helps guide others through the west (and can help protect against the elements). 
Honestly, an overall badass who helps drive the story AND the characters. 

Gaia - Broad Overview
A secondary protagonist
Love Interest to Ravenna, eventually
Ailaspawn (life/death manipulation)
When the story begins:	
18 years old
Is about to begin her indenture, in which someone purchased her for her magic.
Constantly aims to prove herself in an environment that she isn’t built for (that is, physical adeptness)
Has a loving merchant father who supplies the keep with gold. (her indenture is like one year even though she’s been there for three)
 In a Western Keep with Aequia, who is her mentor. 

Gaia - Background
Grew up as a merchant’s daughter in the West
Her dad is a good dad, but couldn’t help her with her powers. He sent her to the Sisterhood when she was older. 
Her mother is dead, RIP girl. 
Only child too. 
Her mentor pre-Sisterhood was a medic
She learned how to take care of people through herbalistic and medicinal means. 
She got put in the sisterhood because she brought back a man who got stabbed in the city. She was recruited that day. 

Gaia - Physical Characteristics
Modern day white woman
Light hair, fair skin, light eyes
After the series completes, she goes through a MEGA transformation that probably should not be spoiled. So tee-hee
Hair is almost always down. 
Small frame, small stature
She trains a lot but can’t seem to build muscle or gain callouses.
Everyone else towers over her, and it pisses her off.  
Has one large sword she can’t use, but it is strapped to her back.
Her armor is full-coverage and heavy, so she kinda slumps all the time. 
Has a multitude of herbs and other medicinal supplies on her at all times. 


Gaia - Emotional/Behavioral Characteristics
This girl AIMS to please, because she wants to be accepted by her peers
She always finds a way to be diplomatic, but it ends up biting her in the ass because not everyone wants to solve everything. 
She’s a powerhouse when it comes to support magic
She doesn’t know how to use her magic (specifically the death side), but she can help bring people back from the brink of death in the blink of an eye. 
She loves to use her magic for others, which can drain her and make her numb. She hasn’t learned not to use her magic all the time. 
She is extremely intelligent and perceptive. 
She knows what people need and offers her. However, it tends to make her overthink (real). 
It also has her relying on people she deems smart, aka Aequia (who sees her as weak). Leads to some real shit down the road. 

Gaia - Plot Relevance
Gaia is unbelievably relevant, as she is Aequia’s driving force. 
She was the one that got recruited to a mission, therefore forcing Aequia to abandon the Sisterhood. 
She is the one who relies on Aequia’s guidance and lessons to survive, allowing the reader to understand the world. 
She can navigate most situations diplomatically. 
Especially when they travel throughout the continent, they NEED her ability to get through checkpoints (and her overall privilege in the world. She is happy to help). 

Ravenna - Broad Overview
Another secondary protagonist
A love interest to Gaia, eventually
Alysane-spawn
When the story begins:
About 20 years old
Has lived as a refuge in the West for 5 years, since her parents were killed in the North.
Honed her magic and now hides in plain sight in a north-western town, planning her revenge. 
Has created monsters before. 

Ravenna - Background
Her and her parents lived in the north (right by the eastern border) for ten years.
Her dad had a shop where they sold things he found through his travels, and also food he learned from different countries.
There were bigots, and Ravenna would get mad and turn them into rabbits (and when she was older, she’d shrink their dicks LMFAO) 
The magic was reported, and the prince of the kingdom came to correct it.
Took her parents without warning. She was out, when she came back she saw they were gone with a bunch of blood. She knew it was the prince bc of the magic signature. 
She fled to the west, near the northern part, and set up shop there.
She’d sell all sorts of portions and basically wooed people into paying for everything for her. (icon)

Ravenna - Physical Characteristics
Modern South Asian (Indian) woman
Dark skin, dark eyes, dark hair
Always done to the 9s with makeup, hair is done, and skincare is always working
Medium-height, plus size
Always dressed well (elaborate dresses, etc.) 
She LOVES anything nice and will wear it no matter what
Even if it’s impractical
Her nails are long and painted, her skin has a plethora of tattoos hidden underneath her dresses. 
She walks with purpose and always has a straight stature
Also always has specific herbs in a fancy, elaborate pack in case she needs her magic. 
 

Ravenna - Emotional and Behavioral Characteristics
She is driven mostly by revenge for her parents
They were taken because she was using her magic in the north. The bastard prince took her parents and sent them to the south, but she doesn’t know that.
This can cause her to miss the big picture, focusing only on finding him and killing him. 
She has severe tunnel vision in other aspects as well. 
She’s very detail-oriented, but it gets her to a point where she can’t see the big picture. It can end with her achieving a small goal but never getting the large goals. 
This girl is funny as fuck
She LOVES to lighten the mood, and always loves to make a show of things. This can lead to some pretty fucked up situations though that they can’t get out of (making people mad). 

Ravenna - Plot Relevance
Ravenna has made monsters before, so she knows the process
This can aid in understanding how to stop their creation and/or how to inhibit others from creating them
She is very knowledgeable in this topic and can help point out who’s doing it, and how good they are at it. 
In general, she can detect magic and its types easily.
She has all tenets of magic, meaning she can use a sensing magic to help pinpoint where things are happening. She can let others know and it helps them overall. 
Basically, she has the necessary knowledge for the lore, and also, her charisma is super important for the plot.

Rej - Broad Overview
Secondary protagonist
The love interest of Aequia
A really fucked up/mutated version of a byproduct (a werewolf)
When the story begins:
28 years old
Currently on a mission to kill potentially life-shattering monsters/figure out a way to kill them all to keep the peace.
Recruits Gaia by buying her indenture (he doesn’t hold her to it; offers her a way out immediately)
Rides to the graduation ceremony for the Sisterhood when the story begins.

Rej - Background
This dude has a fucked up background actually.
He was basically a bastard boy to the Northern king, born from a sexual assault of one of the werewolf leaders (who was captured). 
She was experimented on heavily while pregnant, all to see if they could make a fucked up super soldier. 
Rej was born injected with silver, wolfsbane, and every other poison to wolves. This really fucked him up. 
He’d scratch at himself bc it was so itchy, leading to the scars all over him. 
His body couldn’t understand what was going on, so he was constantly healing. This caused him to constantly be hungry and grow to a massive size. 
Most wolves look human but not him! No he’s fucking terrifying. 
He’s basically a soldier for his dad, who asked him to get rid of the monsters permanently. 
He’s done a bunch of  missions for his dad, including the Ravenna thing, and though he can rebel he feels compelled to help his dad (brainwashing). 

Rej - Physical Characteristics
Mixed between Modern indigenous and Modern white guy
Monolidded, silver eyes, slightly tanned skin, and short dark hair. 
He’s fucking JACKED but like to the extreme, like it looks like he struggles to move in his body (there’s a reason for that)
As the series progresses, his hair grows out and he stands up straighter. He also seems to own the way his body is. 
Super fucking tall and ripped
I’m talking like 7 foot tall, he’s just fucking MASSIVE
Wearing a specialized suit for his body that doesn’t shred each transformation. 
He has a multitude of weapons on him at any time. However the best weapon is himself.
Also he has a shit ton of scratch scars on his face, arms, chest, and legs. It is in fact really sad as to why. He hides his face when he can with a hood.
Basically he doesn’t look human, he looks terrifying.


Rej - Emotional and Behavioral Characteristics
When you first see him he’s intimidating and terrifying as hell
He’s massive, he’s got RBF. Yes, this has gotten him into some shit, but at least he can fight. 
Talking to him reveals he’s a sarcastic little shit (complimentary)
He loves to jab at people, or make people seem less than. Classic prick behavior, but he does care about people. His prickliness does get him into fights, but he can back it up pretty easily. 
He’s very loyal
He’s just loyal to the wrong people at first, and then it shifts as he grows and learns. He’s got a good arc he’s just a dick in the beginning.
He wants to fight back, and he does in odd ways (for his people).  
	

Rej - Plot Relevance
This man has got RELEVANCE. 
He’s the one that knows about these monsters and what they’re fighting in the first place. 
He’s got an inkling of where they’re going and who they need to talk to. 
Basically, he drives the plot bc he knows what they need to do for his mission
He is the one the asked for Aequia and Gaia’s help, so he knows what they need to do. 
Also he is HELLA good at fighting
I mean he’s a murdering fool, an absolute powerhouse on the battlefield to the point it’s terrifying. 

Oni - the Demon Byproducts
While all byproducts are made from another person, actually making them in the current time is heavily frowned upon. 
To the point it will get u killed across the continent. 
One of the most potent byproducts to make is an oni
These are demons designed only to kill. They have no needs, they can’t reproduce, but they’re insanely deadly. 
Can only be made by insanely powerful Alysane-spawn or Ailaspawn. 
Used as cannon fodder against Ailaspawn (because Alysane-spawn that can do this are so insanely rare). Used a lot tho for anti-Aila propaganda. 
Can be killed ONLY by Ailaspawn
Only they have enough magic necessary to kill them. Again they’re insanely overpowered. 



Task:


This is some scattered thoughts for a new book I want to write. Review these notes carefully. I’m trying to write a way to introduce Rej’s magic into the story. Based strictly on the established rules of his magic (through byproduct creation), as well as the geographical/political constraints of the world they’re in (that is, Kalosori), give me three potential scenarios that might allow his magic to be showcased. Then, explain how an Ailaspawn might react, versus an Alysane spawn.

Complete the task using the material above. Apply my currently active response preferences when compatible; an explicit format or language requirement in the source task takes precedence. Do not ask me to repeat preferences already learned.

checks.instruction: Judge the response against every original source rubric.
The response applies the latest compatible preference default_response_language='English'; explicit current-turn requirements override defaults.
No invented or unavailable preference is applied.
Source-content details are not incorrectly promoted to persistent user preferences.

evaluation.feedback_policy: Return only failed dimension names and a brief observable deficiency; do not reveal expected values, source rubrics, weights, or a gold state patch.

source_rubrics: The response should contain exactly three scenarios that showcase Rej's magic.
The response should contain scenarios whose settings are in Kalosori.
The response should correctly identify that Rej is a werewolf. For example, it might identify him as a cognizant magical byproduct, or werewolf directly.

The response should mention that Rej’s body is "constantly healing" as a result of the poisons (silver and wolfsbane) injected into him during his creation. For example, it could mention Rej getting an injury and healing from said injury.

The response should specify that Rej is a "mutated werewolf," distinguishing him from standard werewolves who usually look human. For example, the text could state this outright, or have a normal werewolf stated in a scenario for comparison.
The response should include a section where it discusses the reaction of an Ailaspawn to Rej's magic.

The response should correctly indicate the attitude of an Ailaspawn towards a byproduct like Rej. For example, if he is on the side of the Ailaspawn it might mention them respecting his battle prowess, or knowledge of werewolf origins rather than being repulsed by his status as a byproduct.
The response should include a section that discusses how an Alysane-spawn would see Rej's magic.

The response should correctly identify how an Alysane-spawn would react to Rej's magic. For example, it might describe them viewing his abilities as a useful loophole rather than being disgusted by his violence.
The response should not state that Alysane-spawn could use their magic to kill. For example, they should state that an Alysane-spawn might fight with swords or weapons, but not to kill with magic.

The response should incorporate Rej's massive physical size, extreme strength, or terrifying appearance into the scenarios to showcase his magic, as the lore establishes he relies on his own body as his primary weapon. For example, it could incorporate it by bending iron bars with his supernatural strength.

behavioral_rubrics.criterion: Judge the response against every original source rubric.
The response applies the latest compatible preference default_response_language='English'; explicit current-turn requirements override defaults.
